subject: AeroMed: Request for exec approval - private deployment variance & transient discount
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Deal Desk <dealdesk@redwood.ai>, Legal <legal@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: AeroMed: Request for exec approval - private deployment variance & transient discount

Hi team,

I'm escalating a request for executive sign-off on a special private deployment for AeroMed Analytics (clinical diagnostics startup). They've gone from a pilot to a potential 3-year committed contract, but require a handful of deviations from our standard Private/VPC template to meet their compliance and operational needs. Sales is asking for a temporary concession on list price to lock the multi-year commitment.

Summary of customer asks (see attached MAP and terms draft):
- In-country VPC with monthly in-region audit window (48 hrs notice) and expanded right-to-audit clause beyond SOC 2 (auditor named by customer).
- HSM-backed KMS with customer-supplied keys and a short-term escrow arrangement for cross-certification.
- Site access window that allows their security team occasional remote troubleshooting (read-only session, 3rd-party bastion) — limited to a quarterly 2-hour window.
- A one-time 30% discount on the first 12 months tied to a 36-month committed spend threshold.

Open questions I need approved:
1) Are we willing to accept the expanded right-to-audit language that names an external auditor and allows evidence collection beyond our standard SOC2 artifacts?
2) Approve HSM/KMS customer-supplied keys with an escrow process (redwood still to provide HSM connectivity and key usage logs).
3) Approve the temporary 30% upfront discount for year one only, conditioned on achieving a $1.2M ARR minimum over 36 months.

Customer is sensitive to procurement timelines; they will move the signature to the next board window if we cannot give a quick answer.

Requested action: Legal & Deal Desk — please advise risk/ok buckets. Marissa/Avery — can you provide commercial sign-off if Legal signs off?

Thanks,
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
---
AeroMed_MutualActionPlan.xlsx (attachment stub)
redwood_private_terms_draft_v2.pdf (attachment stub)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>, Deal Desk <dealdesk@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Legal Ops <legalops@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AeroMed: Request for exec approval - private deployment variance & transient discount

Sofia — thanks for the clear summary and attachments. A few legal points up front: 

- Expanded right-to-audit: Naming an external auditor and allowing collection beyond SOC 2 artifacts is a material change. We can accept it with constraints: audits limited to 2x per year, predefined evidence list, and onsite access only with 7 days notice. No access to Redwood internal logs that contain other customer identifiers.

- HSM / customer-provided keys: We can support customer KMS keys in an HSM, but we need an escrow process that is auditable and preserves our support capabilities. Escrow terms must include 3rd-party neutral custodian and a clear trigger/approval workflow.

- Remote troubleshooting sessions: read-only bastion is acceptable if session recording is retained and a joint session owner approves each event. No shell access to host OS; access limited to application-level diagnostics.

- Commercial discount: Legal does not approve commercial discounts; that's for Sales/Finance. We will draft protective language and an indemnity carveout to be appended if the audit scope expands materially.

Please find preliminary redline notes in redwood_private_terms_draft_v2.pdf and the security Q&A attached.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

- We need the signed MSA by July 2 for our Q3 board approval.
- The audit window language must allow our auditor to collect end-to-end evidence for regulatory review (not just service-level artifacts). This is non-negotiable.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Deal Desk <dealdesk@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AeroMed: Request for exec approval - private deployment variance & transient discount

Team — cross-functional ask summarized and recommendation: 

Customer: AeroMed Analytics (pre-revenue clinical AI, strong reference potential in medtech vertical)
Commercial ask: 30% off list for months 1–12, conditioned on 36-month commitment ($1.2M minimum).
Risk mitigations (recommended):
- Limit audit scope to specific evidence catalogue (we propose the SOC2 + supplemental artifacts Karthik outlined).
- Escrow: use neutral custodian; escrow only for emergency unavailability scenarios.
- Session access: quarterly, scheduled, recorded — Redwood to retain recordings for 90 days.

Recommendation: Approve the deployment variance and transient discount with the above constraints. Reason: strategic medtech vertical entry + long-term ARR with renewable options. Financial impact model attached (brief).

Asks for Execs: 
1) Avery — can you approve a one-time commercialization concession of up to 30% for year one, contingent on the $1.2M 36-month commit and final legal sign-off?
2) Finance — confirm the revenue recognition approach and required billing holdbacks (if any).

If we get a green light today we will finalize the DocuSign and push for a July 1 signature.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
VP, Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: AeroMed: Request for exec approval - private deployment variance & transient discount

Marissa / team — approve the exceptions with these binding conditions: 

1) Discount: Up to 30% for months 1–12 only, paid as standard invoices. Discount clawback if customer fails to reach $1.2M committed ARR within 36 months; clawback mechanics to be defined by Finance (pro-rate and invoice the difference).
2) Audit: Accept limited external auditor rights per Karthik, capped to two audits/year, predefined evidence list, and 7 days notice. No access to cross-customer logs; any additional requests escalate to Legal + Execs.
3) KMS/HSM: Approve customer-supplied keys and escrow via neutral third-party custodian. Redwood to maintain usage logs and document key usage.
4) Session access: Approve quarterly 2-hour read-only troubleshooting sessions. Sessions must be scheduled 7 days in advance, recorded, and retained for 90 days.

Condition: Legal to sign the final redlines (Karthik) and Finance to confirm billing/clawback text. Once Legal provides final PSAs, Deal Desk to prepare DocuSign.

Sofia / Marissa — proceed on my approval and get this executed; keep me posted on final signed copy.

Avery Johnson
Chief Revenue Officer (acting), Redwood Inference
